Toyota Cuts Tacoma's Free Maintenance in Half for Model Year 2027
17 photos
Photo: Toyota
Under the 2026 model year ToyotaCare plan for the Tacoma, the mid-size pickup enjoyed factory-scheduled maintenance for two years or 25,000 miles, whichever comes first. Upgrading to the 2027 model is actually a downgrade from this point of view, for Toyota Motor North America has reduced coverage to one year or 10,000 miles. In other words, two instead of four potential complimentary visits.
A substantial reduction, for sure, but what rattles me is how Toyota's announcement makes a poor effort to communicate it. The media release detailing the 2027 model year Tacoma for the US market spends page after page explaining new convenience features, off-road equipment, and infotainment stuff. Only at the end of said release, the maintenance plan gets a single sentence.
One sentence, yes, and Toyota Motor North America couldn't be bothered to explain this reduction.
More curiously, TMNA didn't even compare it with the outgoing arrangement or flag it among the headline changes for 2027. While the manufacturer cannot be accused of concealing the new coverage, stripping the relevant numbers of the context needed to understand what customers are losing isn't a good look at all.
The downgrade becomes more evident when the actual mileage schedule is considered. Toyota recommends scheduling maintenance every 5,000 miles or six months, with routine visits including fluid level checks, tire rotations, and inspections of the chassis, brakes, and wipers. Oil and filter replacement is recommended every 10,000 miles or 12 months under normal driving conditions.
Under the 2026 model year ToyotaCare arrangement for the US market, customers who followed the calendar-based schedule could receive up to four services over two years. The new plan covers two. Adding insult to injury, the general ToyotaCare brochure illustrates an oil and filter change at six and 12 months even though its footnote informs customers that service requirements vary by model.
Photo: Toyota Removing the 24-month visit from the complimentary period means that customers lose the second normally scheduled oil and filter replacement. If you're good at math, you might have also noticed that the mileage allowance has fallen by 60 rather than 50 percent. Toyota 's presentation of the change makes it all the more irritating.
The Japanese automaker cites customer feedback when explaining why the 14-inch media system is being made easier to configure, then describes revised packaging as a value improvement. Yet it offers no comparable explanation for removing a year and 15,000 miles of scheduled maintenance. What gives?
Toyota Motor North America is offsetting costs this way, namely production and tariff costs. As you're well aware, all Tacos produced for model year 2027 hail from Mexico. That means all 2027 models are tariffed at 25 percent under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, and this levy eats into Toyota's margin.
Absorbing the tariff, therefore, can be considered a major driver behind the ToyotaCare downgrade. Even so, we also have to consider parts and labor inflation. That being said, imagine saving $250 per truck in dealer reimbursements by cutting three dealership visits. $250 times 274,638 Tacomas delivered in the US last year is a lot of money, and it's rather pitiful that it has come to this.
